verdict.rationale: This transaction exhibits a classic structuring pattern: a cash deposit of $4,950 USD—just $50 below the $5,000 reporting threshold—following two similar sub-threshold deposits. Hybrid search identified five nearly identical precedent cases (txn-syn-00016, txn-syn-00024, txn-syn-00039, txn-syn-00042, txn-syn-00047), all flagged as structuring and escalated. Each precedent involved deposits in the $4,900–$4,998 range, all just under the $5,000 threshold, and all part of repeated sequential patterns within the same week or period. The deliberate pattern of splitting cash into multiple sub-reporting-threshold deposits is a hallmark indicator of structuring ("smurfing"), an anti-money laundering red flag designed to evade currency transaction reporting. Fund tracing did not reveal circular flow or layering patterns, but this does not diminish the structuring concern—the pattern itself is the primary risk signal.
